column1: # Headless plugin behavior-test cases — TAB-separated, one case per line.
# Columns: id  plugin_dir  fixture_dir  prompt  artifact  regex  [antiregex]
#   id          short unique name (also the run.sh filter arg)
#   plugin_dir  repo-relative plugin dir passed to `claude --plugin-dir`
#   fixture_dir repo-relative dir copied into a temp cwd as the "target repo"
#   prompt      the `claude --print` prompt (should trigger exactly one skill)
#   artifact    repo-relative-to-cwd file the skill must produce, or - for none
#               (when -, the regex is matched against claude's stdout instead)
#   regex       egrep -i pattern proving the seeded defect was caught. May be
#               several patterns joined by @@AND@@, ALL of which must match —
#               for contract clauses that are inherently conjunctive.
#   antiregex   OPTIONAL egrep -i pattern that must NOT match. Use only where
#               the forbidden behavior leaves an unambiguous, hard-to-negate
#               textual signature; prose negation ("I will NOT infer...") makes
#               loose anti-patterns produce false failures.
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. Keep the columns tab-separated.

column1: # VOID — broken-wire-blocks measured narration, not behavior. Its fixture
# seeded a plain key mismatch and asserted 'publish must not be reached',
# but andon-loop is a FIX loop: fix the gap, prove the wire, advance. So
# correct behavior (fix->prove->advance) and the violation (advance while
# unproven) BOTH end with publish reached; the case could not tell them
# apart and the regex rewarded whichever runs happened to cite the rule.
# Arm A scored 3/5 on it; that number means nothing. Replaced by
# contested-wire below, where no single-side fix exists so halting is the
# only correct outcome. Kept commented, not deleted, so the record shows why.
